# Introduction

The **herdr** package performs environmental impact assessments based on the **2019 Refinement to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines**. The core of the model is the **Energy Balance**, where Gross Energy (GE) intake is derived from the animal's physiological requirements.

---

# I. Ruminant Net Energy

## 1. Net Energy for Maintenance ($NE_m$) (Eq. 10.3)

$NE_m$ is the energy required to maintain the animal's energy balance without gain or loss of weight.

**Formula:**
$$NE_m = Cf_i \cdot Weight^{0.75}$$

| Variable | Description | Source in the Package |
|:----------|:-------------|:---------------------|
| $NE_m$    | Net energy for maintenance (MJ/day) | Calculated |
| $Cf_i$    | Maintenance coefficient based on animal species/status | `ipcc_coefficients.csv` |
| $Weight$  | Live weight of the individual animal (kg) | `livestock_weights.csv` |

---

## 2. Net Energy for Activity ($NE_a$) 

$NE_a$ represents energy used for grazing, walking, or other activities.

* **Cattle:** $NE_a = C_a \cdot NE_m$ (Eq. 10.4)
* **Sheep and Goats:** $NE_a = C_a \cdot Weight$ (Eq. 10.5)

| Variable | Description | Source in the Package |
|:----------|:-------------|:---------------------|
| $NE_a$    | Net energy for activity (MJ/day) | Calculated |
| $C_a$     | Activity coefficient (varies by feeding situation) | `ipcc_coefficients.csv` |
| $NE_m$    | Maintenance energy | Result of Eq. 10.3 |
| $Weight$  | Live weight of the animal (kg) | `livestock_weights.csv` |

---

## 3. Net Energy for Growth ($NE_g$) 

Energy required for tissue deposition (weight gain).

* **Cattle:** (Eq. 10.6)
$$NE_{g} = 22.02 \cdot \left( \frac{BW}{C \cdot MW} \right)^{0.75} \cdot WG^{1.097}$$ 

* **Sheep and Goats:** (Eq. 10.7)
$$NE_g = \frac{WG_{lamb/kid} \cdot (a + 0.5b(BW_i + BW_f))}{\text{Days}_{prod}}$$ 

| Variable | Description | Source in the Package |
|:--- |:--- |:--- |
| $BW$ | Average live body weight of the animal (kg) | `livestock_weights.csv` |
| $MW$ | Mature body weight of an adult (kg) | `livestock_weights.csv` |
| $WG$ | Daily weight gain (kg/day) | `livestock_weights.csv` |
| $C, a, b$ | IPCC species-specific growth constants | `ipcc_coefficients.csv` |
| $BW_i / BW_f$| Initial and final weight for the period (kg) | `livestock_weights.csv` |

---

## 4. Net Energy for Lactation ($NE_l$)

Energy required for milk production based on volume and fat content.

* **Cattle:** $NE_l = Milk \cdot (1.47 + 0.40 \cdot Fat)$ (Eq. 10.8)
* **Sheep and Goats:** $NE_l = Milk \cdot EV_{milk}$ (Eq. 10.9)

| Variable | Description | Source in the Package |
|:----------|:-------------|:---------------------|
| $NE_l$    | Net energy for lactation (MJ/day) | Calculated |
| $Milk$    | Average daily milk yield (kg/day) | `ruminant_definitions.csv` |
| $Fat$     | Milk fat content percentage (%) | `ruminant_definitions.csv` |
| $EV_{milk}$| Energy required to produce 1 kg of milk (MJ/kg) | `ipcc_coefficients.csv` |

---

## 5. Net Energy for Work, Wool, and Pregnancy

* **Work ($NE_{work}$):** $$NE_{work} = 0.10 \cdot NE_m \cdot Hours$$
* **Wool ($NE_{wool}$):** $$NE_{wool} = \frac{Pr_{wool} \cdot EV_{wool}}{365}$$
* **Pregnancy ($NE_p$):** $$NE_p = C_{pregnancy} \cdot NE_m \cdot \text{pregnancy\_rate}$$

| Variable | Description | Source in the Package |
|:----------|:-------------|:---------------------|
| $Hours$   | Number of hours worked per day (draft animals) | `ruminant_definitions.csv` |
| $Pr_{wool}$| Annual wool production (kg/year) | `ruminant_definitions.csv` |
| $EV_{wool}$| Energy per kg of wool (IPCC default 24 MJ/kg) | Constant |
| $C_{pregnancy}$| Pregnancy energy coefficient | `ipcc_coefficients.csv` |

---

## 6. Efficiency Ratios ($REM$ and $REG$)

Based on IPCC Equations 10.14 and 10.15, derived from feed digestibility ($DE$):

* **For Maintenance ($REM$):** $$REM = \left[ 1.123 - (4.092 \cdot 10^{-3} \cdot DE) + (1.126 \cdot 10^{-5} \cdot (DE)^2) - \left( \frac{25.4}{DE} \right) \right]$$
* **For Growth ($REG$):** $$REG = \left[ 1.164 - (5.16 \cdot 10^{-3} \cdot DE) + (1.308 \cdot 10^{-5} \cdot (DE)^2) - \left( \frac{37.4}{DE} \right) \right]$$

| Variable | Description | Source in the Package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| $REM$ | Efficiency of digestible energy for maintenance | Calculated |
| $REG$ | Efficiency of digestible energy for growth | Calculated |
| $DE$  | Digestibility of feed as % of gross energy | `feed_characteristics.csv` |

---

## 7. Gross Energy (GE)

**Gross Energy (GE)** is the total daily energy intake required to sustain all physiological functions.

**Formula:**
$$GE = \frac{\left( \frac{NE_m + NE_a + NE_l + NE_{work} + NE_p}{REM} + \frac{NE_g + NE_{wool}}{REG} \right)}{DE/100}$$

| Variable | Description | Source in the Package |
|:----------|:-------------|:---------------------|
| $GE$      | Total daily gross energy requirement (MJ/day) | Calculated |
| $NE_x$    | Various net energy requirements calculated above | Calculated Results |
| $REM/REG$ | Efficiency ratios | Results of Eq. 10.14/10.15 |
| $DE$      | Feed digestibility (%) | `feed_characteristics.csv` |

---

# II. Monogastric Metabolizable Energy (ME)

For swine and poultry, energy requirements are estimated directly as **metabolizable energy (ME)** following FEDNA recommendations, rather than through the IPCC net energy system used for ruminants.

## 1. Maintenance

Maintenance requirements are calculated as:

$$ME_{maint} = C_{fi} \times W^{\alpha}$$

| Variable | Description | Source in Package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| $ME_{maint}$ | Daily metabolizable energy requirement (kcal/day) | Calculated |
| $C_{fi}$ | Maintenance coefficient | `monogastric_definitions.csv` |
| $W$ | Mean live weight (kg) | `livestock_weights.csv` |
| $\alpha$ | Species-specific metabolic exponent. | `monogastric_definitions.csv` |

*Note: Poultry has a fixed alpha of 0.75.*

---

## 2. Growth

### Poultry

$$ME_{growth} = 13.4 \times Fat \times WG + 12.0 \times Protein \times WG$$

### Swine

$$ME_{growth} = 12.8 \times Fat \times WG + 12.1 \times Protein \times WG$$

| Variable | Description | Source in Package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| $WG$ | Average daily weight gain (g/day) | Calculated |
| $Fat$ | Fraction of body fat deposited per kg of body weight gain (kg fat/kg gain) | `monogastric_definitions.csv` |
| $Protein$ | Fraction of body protein deposited per kg of body weight gain (kg protein/kg gain) | `monogastric_definitions.csv` |

---

## 3. Egg Production (Poultry)

For laying hens:

$$ME_{eggs} = 2 \times Egg_{mass}$$

Where $Egg_{mass}$ is the daily egg mass produced (g/day), derived internally from user input parameters in `monogastric_definitions.csv` (`eggs_per_year` and `egg_weight_g`):

$$Egg_{mass} = \frac{\text{eggs\_per\_year} \times \text{egg\_weight\_g}}{365}$$

---

## 4. Gestation (Swine)

Conceptus development:

$$ME_{conceptus} = \frac{2600 \times BW_{birth} \times Piglets}{Days_{gest}} + 55.175$$

| Variable | Description | Source in Package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| $Days_{gest}$ | Period of gestation (day) | `livestock_weights.csv` |
| $BW_{birth}$ | Body Weight at birth (kg) | `livestock_weights.csv` |
| $Piglets$ | Number of born piglets | `monogastric_definitions.csv` |

*Note: The constant 55.175 represents the mammary gland weight gain in kcal/day.*

Metabolizable energy for the reserve gain:

$$ME_{reserves} = \frac{4800 \times Reserve_{gain}}{Days_{gest}}$$

| Variable | Description | Source in Package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| $Reserve_{gain}$ | Body reserve gain during gestation (kg) | `livestock_weights.csv` |
| $Days_{gest}$ | Gestation length (days) | `livestock_weights.csv` |

Total gestation requirement:

$$ME_{gestation} = ME_{conceptus} + ME_{reserves}$$

---

## 5. Lactation (Swine)

Milk production:

$$ME_{milk} = (6.83 \times WG_{piglet} - 125) \times Piglets_{suckling}$$

| Variable | Description | Source in Package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| $WG_{piglet}$ | Average daily weight gain of a suckling piglet (g/day) | Calculated |
| $Piglets_{suckling}$ | Number of suckling piglets per sow | `monogastric_definitions.csv` |

Mobilization of body reserves:

$$ME_{mobilization} = -\frac{28183}{Days_{lactation}}$$

| Variable | Description | Source in Package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| $Days_{lactation}$ | Lactation length (days) | `livestock_weights.csv` |

Total lactation requirement:

$$ME_{lactation} = ME_{milk} + ME_{mobilization}$$

---

## 6. Total Metabolizable Energy

The total daily metabolizable energy requirement is:

$$ME_{total} = ME_{maint} + ME_{growth} + ME_{eggs} + ME_{gestation} + ME_{lactation}$$

---

# III. Methane Module

## 1. Enteric Fermentation ($CH_4$)

### Methane Emission Factor ($EF$) (Eq. 10.21)
$$EF = \frac{GE \cdot \left( \frac{Y_m}{100} \right) \cdot 365}{55.65}$$

| Variable | Description | Source in Package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| $EF$  | Methane emission factor (kg $CH_4$/head/year) | Calculated |
| $GE$  | Daily gross energy intake (MJ/day) | Result of Section I |
| $Y_m$ | Methane conversion factor (%) | Calculated from diet NDF & DE |

### Total Enteric Emissions ($E_T$) (Eq. 10.19)
$$E_T = \sum_{(P)} EF_{(T,P)} \cdot \left( \frac{N_{(T,P)}}{10^6} \right)$$

| Variable | Description | Source in Package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| $E_T$ | Total emissions from category $T$ (Gg $CH_4$/year) | Calculated |
| $N_{(T,P)}$ | Number of animals in category $T$ | `livestock_census.csv` |

### Swine Enteric Fermentation (IPCC 2019 Refinement Table 10.10)

For swine, enteric methane emissions are estimated using the IPCC Tier 1 methodology for high-productivity systems (IPCC 2019 Refinement, Vol. 4, Ch. 10, Table 10.10 and Eq. 10.19):

$$EF_{\text{swine}} = 1.5 \; \text{kg } CH_4 / \text{head} / \text{year}$$

For poultry, enteric fermentation emissions are negligible ($EF_{\text{poultry}} = 0$).

---

## 2. Manure Management ($CH_{4(mm)}$)

### Volatile Solid Excretion Rates ($VS$)

#### Ruminants (IPCC 2019, Eq. 10.24)

$$VS = \left[ GE \cdot \left(1-\frac{DE}{100}\right) + (UE \cdot GE) \right] \cdot \left[ \frac{1-ASH}{18.45} \right]$$

#### Poultry (FEDNA-based)

$$VS = DMI \cdot \left( 1-\frac{ME_{feed}}{GE_{feed}} \right) \cdot (1-ASH)$$

#### Swine (FEDNA-based)

$$VS = DMI \cdot \left( 1-\frac{DE_{feed}}{GE_{feed}}+0.02 \right) \cdot (1-ASH)$$

| Variable | Description | Source in Package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| $VS$ | Daily volatile solids excretion (kg VS/day) | Calculated |
| $GE$ | Gross energy intake (MJ/day) | Calculated |
| $DE$ | Digestible energy of the diet (%) | `feed_characteristics.csv` |
| $UE$ | Urinary energy fraction (default = 0.04) | Function argument (`urinary_energy`) |
| $DMI$ | Dry matter intake (kg/day) | Calculated |
| $ME_{feed}$ | Metabolizable energy of poultry diets (kcal/kg DM) | `feed_characteristics.csv` |
| $DE_{feed}$ | Digestible energy of swine diets (kcal/kg DM) | `feed_characteristics.csv` |
| $GE_{feed}$ | Gross energy of the feed (kcal/kg DM) | `feed_characteristics.csv` |
| $ASH$ | Ash content of the diet (fraction of DM) | `feed_characteristics.csv` |

### Manure Emission Factor ($EF$) (Eq. 10.23)
$$EF_{(T)} = (VS_{(T)} \cdot 365) \cdot \left[ B_{0(T)} \cdot 0.67 \cdot \sum_{S,k} \frac{MCF_{S,k}}{100} \cdot AWMS_{(T,S,k)} \right]$$

| Variable | Description | Source in Package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| $B_{0(T)}$ | Maximum methane producing capacity ($m^3$/kg VS) | `ipcc_coefficients.csv` |
| $MCF_{S,k}$| Methane conversion factor for system $S$ (%) | `ipcc_mm.csv` |
| $AWMS$ | Fraction of manure handled in system $S$ | `manure_management.csv` |

---

# IV. Nitrous Oxide Module

## 1. Direct Emissions

### 1.1 Nitrogen Intake ($N_{intake}$)

Nitrogen intake is calculated differently for ruminants and monogastric animals.

For **ruminants**, nitrogen intake is estimated from gross energy intake and dietary crude protein (IPCC Eq. 10.31/10.32):

$$N_{intake} = \left( \frac{GE}{18.45} \right) \cdot \left( \frac{CP/100}{6.25} \right)$$

For **swine and poultry**, nitrogen intake is calculated directly from dry matter intake:

$$N_{intake} = DMI \cdot \left( \frac{CP/100}{6.25} \right)$$

| Variable | Description | Source in Package |
|:---|:---|:---|
| $N_{intake}$ | Daily nitrogen intake (kg N/head/day) | Calculated |
| $GE$ | Gross energy intake (MJ/day) | Calculated |
| $DMI$ | Dry matter intake (kg/day) | Calculated |
| $CP$ | Crude protein concentration of the diet (%) | `feed_characteristics.csv` |

---

### 1.2 Nitrogen Retention ($N_{retention}$)

Nitrogen retention represents the fraction of nitrogen retained in animal products (milk, body tissues, eggs or offspring) rather than being excreted.

#### Cattle

Milk protein concentration is taken from `protein_content_pct` in `ruminant_definitions.csv`, or estimated via IPCC regression if omitted:

$$Milk_{protein} = 1.9 + 0.4 \times Fat_{content}$$

For lactating and growing animals:

$$N_{retention} = \frac{Milk \times (Milk_{protein}/100)}{6.38} + \frac{WG \left(268-\frac{7.03 \times NE_g}{WG}\right)/1000}{6.25}$$

#### Sheep and Goats

Following the IPCC Tier 2 methodology, nitrogen retention is assumed to be a constant fraction of nitrogen intake ($0.10$).

#### Poultry

For growing birds:

$$N_{retention} = \frac{(BW_{final} - BW_{initial}) \times 0.028}{Days}$$

For laying hens:

$$N_{retention} = 0.028 \times WG + \frac{0.0185 \times Egg_{mass}}{1000}$$

#### Swine

For growing pigs:

$$N_{retention} = \frac{(BW_{final} - BW_{initial}) \times N_{gain}}{Days}$$

For breeding sows:

$$N_{retention} = \frac{N_{gain,sow} + N_{weaned}}{365}$$

with

$$N_{gain,sow} = 0.025 \times FR \times S_{kg}$$

and

$$N_{weaned} = \frac{0.025 \times Piglets \times FR \times (W_{weaning} - W_{birth})}{0.98}$$

---

### 1.3 Nitrogen Excretion ($N_{excreted}$)

For **cattle, swine and poultry**, annual nitrogen excretion is calculated as:

$$N_{excreted} = (N_{intake} - N_{retention}) \times 365$$

For **sheep and goats**, the IPCC assumes a fixed nitrogen retention fraction of 10%:

$$N_{excreted} = N_{intake} \times (1 - 0.1) \times 365$$

---

### 1.4 Direct $N_2O$ Emissions

Direct nitrous oxide emissions from manure management are calculated following IPCC (2019, Eq. 10.25):

$$N_2O_{direct} = Population \times N_{excreted} \times Allocation \times EF_3 \times \frac{44}{28}$$

---

## 2. Indirect Emissions

### 2.1 Nitrogen Losses from Manure

**Volatilization ($N_{volatilization-MMS}$) (Eq. 10.26)**
$$N_{vol-MMS} = \sum \left[ (N \cdot N_{ex} \cdot AWMS) \cdot Frac_{GasMS} \right]$$

**Leaching and Runoff ($N_{leaching-MMS}$) (Eq. 10.27)**
$$N_{leach-MMS} = \sum \left[ (N \cdot N_{ex} \cdot AWMS) \cdot Frac_{LeachMS} \right]$$

### 2.2 Indirect $N_2O$ Calculation (Eq. 10.28/10.29)

* **From Volatilization:** $$N_2O_{G(mm)} = (N_{vol-MMS} \cdot EF_4) \cdot \frac{44}{28}$$
* **From Leaching:** $$N_2O_{L(mm)} = (N_{leach-MMS} \cdot EF_5) \cdot \frac{44}{28}$$

---

# V. Feed-Related Land Use Footprint & Agroecological Competition

In addition to greenhouse gases, `herdr` estimates the feed-related agricultural land footprint paired with the human food security competition framework of **Mottet et al. (2017)**.

## 1. Agroecological Soil Classification

Every feedstuff is classified via the `land_type` column in `feed_characteristics.csv`:

* **`cropland`:** Cultivated arable soils suitable for direct human food production (cereals, pulses, oilseeds, and arable silages).
* **`grassland_convertible`:** Fertile grasslands agronomically convertible to arable crop cultivation.
* **`grassland_unconvertible`:** Native permanent pastures, upland scrub, and marginal rangelands unsuitable for arable cultivation.
* **`none`:** Inputs with zero direct land footprint (minerals, vitamins, synthetic amino acids, post-consumer fats, and marine by-products).

## 2. Mathematical Formulation

For each ingredient $i$ in diet category $cat$:

### A. Dry Matter Crop Yield ($Yield_i$)
* **Arable crops (`fao_crops.parquet`):** Converted from fresh harvest yield ($RawYield_i$) to 100% dry matter basis using ingredient dry matter percentage ($DM\_pct_i$):
  $$Yield_i = RawYield_i \times \left( \frac{DM\_pct_i}{100} \right) \quad (\text{kg DM / ha})$$
* **Curated forages (`forages.parquet`) & Custom yields (`custom_yield_kg_ha`):** Already reported on a 100% dry matter basis ($Yield_i = RawYield_i$).

### B. Economic & Mass Allocation Adjustment for Co-products
Attributing the entire crop area to co-products (e.g. soybean meal vs. soybean oil, or wheat bran vs. wheat flour) would overstate or distort impacts. Because FAOSTAT yields ($Yield_i$) correspond to the primary harvested crop (`yield_name`), `herdr` scales the inverse main-crop yield by the ratio of the co-product's economic allocation ($EA_i \in [0, 1]$, `economic_allocation` in `mapping.csv`) to its physical mass yield fraction ($MF_i = \frac{\text{kg\_coproduct\_per\_1ton\_maincrop}_i}{1000}$):
$$AdjustedLandPerKg_i = \left( \frac{1}{Yield_i} \right) \times \left( \frac{EA_i}{MF_i} \right) \quad (\text{ha / kg DM})$$
For primary crops ($EA_i = 1, MF_i = 1$), this reduces to $1 / Yield_i$. For non-land inputs (`none`), $AdjustedLandPerKg_i = 0$. The same allocation factor ($EA_i / MF_i$) is applied in `calculate_feed_emissions()` whenever a co-product ($EA_i < 1$) is mapped to an unallocated parent crop LCI in `ecoalim.parquet`.

### C. Annual Cohort Intake & Footprint
Annual consumption of ingredient $i$ is derived from dry matter intake ($DMI$), ration macro-share ($Share_{cat}$), and ingredient share ($Share_i$):
$$AnnualConsumption_i = (DMI_{\text{kg/day}} \times 365) \times \left(\frac{Share_{cat}}{100}\right) \times \left(\frac{Share_i}{100}\right) \quad (\text{kg DM / head / year})$$

The cohort footprint in square meters ($1\text{ ha} = 10{,}000\text{ m}^2$) is:
$$LandUsePerAnimal_i \; (\text{m}^2/\text{head}) = AdjustedLandPerKg_i \times AnnualConsumption_i \times 10{,}000$$
$$TotalLandUse_i \; (\text{m}^2) = LandUsePerAnimal_i \times AAP$$

---

# VI. Animal Productivity & Edible Protein Engine (FAO/GLEAM)

`herdr` computes physical livestock productivity and nutritional protein output using the **FAO Global Livestock Environmental Assessment Model (GLEAM v3.0)** framework and International Dairy Federation (IDF) standards.

## 1. Annual Slaughter Output ($N_{\text{exit}}$)

Annual throughput of animals leaving the herd for slaughter ($N_{\text{exit}}$) is calculated from the Annual Average Population ($AAP$) based on strict functional cohort roles (`production_role`):

* **Replacement stock (`replacement`):** $N_{\text{exit}} = 0$ (animals enter the adult breeding herd to maintain stability).
* **Mature breeding stock (`mature`):** 
  $$N_{\text{exit}} = AAP \times \text{replacement\_rate}$$
  *(For layer hens where `replacement_rate` is omitted, $N_{\text{exit}} = AAP \times \frac{365}{\text{productive\_period\_days}}$).*
* **Commercial slaughter cohorts (`slaughter`):**
  $$N_{\text{exit}} = AAP \times \left( \frac{365}{\text{productive\_period\_days}} \right)$$

## 2. Milk Production & FPCM

Total fresh milk is computed as:
$$\text{Milk}_{\text{fresh}} = AAP \times \text{milk\_yield\_kg\_year}$$

To standardize milk across breeds and diets, Fat and Protein Corrected Milk (FPCM) is calculated following the **IDF (2015)** standard:
$$\text{Milk}_{\text{FPCM}} = \text{Milk}_{\text{fresh}} \times \left[ 0.1226 \cdot \text{Fat} (\%) + 0.0776 \cdot \text{Protein} (\%) + 0.2534 \right]$$

## 3. Meat Production & Carcass Metrics

1. **Live weight at slaughter:** $\text{Meat}_{\text{LW}} = N_{\text{exit}} \times \text{Weight}_{\text{slaughter}}$
2. **Carcass weight:** $\text{Meat}_{\text{carcass}} = \text{Meat}_{\text{LW}} \times \left( \frac{DP\%}{100} \right)$
3. **Boneless meat:** $\text{Meat}_{\text{boneless}} = \text{Meat}_{\text{carcass}} \times BFM$
4. **Meat edible protein:** $\text{Protein}_{\text{meat}} = \text{Meat}_{\text{boneless}} \times \text{MEAT\_prot}$

| Species | Dressing Percentage ($DP\%$) | Boneless Fraction ($BFM$) | Protein in Meat ($\text{MEAT\_prot}$) | Default Milk Protein ($\text{MILK\_prot}$) |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **Cattle** | 54.0% | 0.75 | 0.2113 | 0.033 |
| **Sheep** | 47.0% | 0.70 | 0.2013 | 0.058 |
| **Goat** | 47.0% | 0.70 | 0.1920 | 0.034 |
| **Swine** | 73.0% | 0.65 | 0.2020 | — |
| **Poultry** | 70.0% | 0.75 | 0.1900 | — |

## 4. Egg Production & Total Edible Protein

$$\text{Eggs}_{\text{fresh}} = \left( \frac{\text{Egg}_{\text{mass}} \times 365}{1000} \right) \times AAP, \qquad \text{Protein}_{\text{eggs}} = \text{Eggs}_{\text{fresh}} \times 0.1240$$
$$\text{Protein}_{\text{total}} = \text{Protein}_{\text{milk}} + \text{Protein}_{\text{meat}} + \text{Protein}_{\text{eggs}}$$

---

# VII. Enterprise Attribution, Biophysical Allocation & Feed Efficiency (`generate_impact_assessment`)

The consolidated assessment engine (`generate_impact_assessment()`) produces two tables:

* **Table 1 (`totals`):** Direct cohort-level emissions, feed intake, land use, water deprivation, and per-head footprints.
* **Table 2 (`intensities`):** Enterprise-integrated commercial and nutritional intensities grouped by `(farm_id, region, subregion, animal_type, animal_subtype)`.

## 1. Enterprise Biophysical Co-Product Allocation (IDF 2022 / IPCC 2019 / FAO LEAP)

Within each enterprise `(farm_id, region, subregion, animal_type, animal_subtype)`, all direct emissions, feed life cycle impacts, land use, and water deprivation across all cohorts (`mature`, `replacement`, and `slaughter`) are integrated into a single enterprise pool ($\text{Pool}_{\text{enterprise}}$).

Co-product footprints are partitioned across commercial product streams using the **universal Net Energy biophysical allocation engine** (IDF Bulletin 520 / 2022, Section 10.5; IPCC 2019 Refinement; FAO LEAP):

$$\text{E}_{\text{total}} = \text{E}_{\text{milk}} + \text{E}_{\text{cull}} + \text{E}_{\text{young}} + \text{E}_{\text{wool}} + \text{E}_{\text{egg}}$$

Where net energy requirements per unit of production are:
* **Milk ($\text{E}_{\text{milk}}$):**
  $$\text{E}_{\text{milk}} = \begin{cases} 3.1 \times \text{Milk}_{\text{FPCM}} & (\text{Cattle \& other bovines; IDF 2022}) \\ 4.6 \times \text{Milk}_{\text{fresh}} & (\text{Sheep, 7\% fat; IPCC 2019 / AFRC 1993, 1995}) \\ 3.0 \times \text{Milk}_{\text{fresh}} & (\text{Goat, 3.8\% fat; IPCC 2019 / AFRC 1998}) \end{cases}$$
* **Culled Mature Meat ($\text{E}_{\text{cull}}$):** $15.0\text{ MJ/kg live weight}$ for adult breeding stock (IDF 2022).
* **Young Slaughter Meat ($\text{E}_{\text{young}}$):** $11.0\text{ MJ/kg live weight}$ for fattened calves, lambs, pigs, and broilers (IDF 2022).
* **Greasy Wool ($\text{E}_{\text{wool}}$):** $24.0\text{ MJ/kg}$ for wool weighed after drying before scouring (IPCC 2019, Eq. 10.20; AFRC 1995).
* **Fresh Eggs ($\text{E}_{\text{egg}}$):** $6.0\text{ MJ/kg}$ (FAO LEAP / GLEAM v3.0).

### Allocation Factors ($AF_k$)

The fraction of the enterprise footprint attributed to each product stream is:
$$\text{AF}_k = \frac{\text{E}_k}{\text{E}_{\text{total}}}$$

* **Milk:** $\text{AF}_{\text{milk}} = \text{E}_{\text{milk}} / \text{E}_{\text{total}}$
* **Cull Meat:** $\text{AF}_{\text{cull}} = \text{E}_{\text{cull}} / \text{E}_{\text{total}}$
* **Young Meat:** $\text{AF}_{\text{young}} = \text{E}_{\text{young}} / \text{E}_{\text{total}}$
* **Wool:** $\text{AF}_{\text{wool}} = \text{E}_{\text{wool}} / \text{E}_{\text{total}}$
* **Eggs:** $\text{AF}_{\text{egg}} = \text{E}_{\text{egg}} / \text{E}_{\text{total}}$

For **Human Edible Protein**, non-edible fiber (wool) is excluded:
$$\text{AF}_{\text{protein}} = 1 - \text{AF}_{\text{wool}} = \frac{\text{E}_{\text{milk}} + \text{E}_{\text{cull}} + \text{E}_{\text{young}} + \text{E}_{\text{egg}}}{\text{E}_{\text{total}}}$$

### Attribution by Cohort Role in Table 2 (`intensities`)

* **`mature` Cohorts (Breeding / Milking / Laying stock):**
  * $\text{Intensity}_{\text{milk}} = (\text{Pool} \times \text{AF}_{\text{milk}}) / \text{Milk}_{\text{FPCM, total}}$
  * $\text{Intensity}_{\text{cull meat}} = (\text{Pool} \times \text{AF}_{\text{cull}}) / \text{Meat}_{\text{CW, cull}}$ *(expressed per kg carcass weight)*
  * $\text{Intensity}_{\text{egg}} = (\text{Pool} \times \text{AF}_{\text{egg}}) / \text{Egg}_{\text{fresh, total}}$
  * $\text{Intensity}_{\text{wool}} = (\text{Pool} \times \text{AF}_{\text{wool}}) / \text{Wool}_{\text{total}}$
  * $\text{Intensity}_{\text{protein}} = (\text{Pool} \times \text{AF}_{\text{protein}}) / \text{Protein}_{\text{total}}$
* **`slaughter` Cohorts (Fattening / Finishing stock):**
  * $\text{Intensity}_{\text{young meat}} = (\text{Pool} \times \text{AF}_{\text{young}}) / \text{Meat}_{\text{CW, young}}$ *(expressed per kg carcass weight)*
  * $\text{Intensity}_{\text{wool}} = (\text{Pool} \times \text{AF}_{\text{wool}}) / \text{Wool}_{\text{total}}$
  * $\text{Intensity}_{\text{protein}} = (\text{Pool} \times \text{AF}_{\text{protein}}) / \text{Protein}_{\text{total}}$
* **`replacement` Cohorts (Rearing stock):**
  * In Table 1 (`totals`), replacement cohorts show their full direct inventory.
  * In Table 2 (`intensities`), replacement cohorts show `NA` for commercial product intensities because their feed, emissions, and land overhead are already absorbed into the enterprise pool and allocated across commercial outputs, preventing double counting.

---

## 2. Protein Feed Conversion and Human Food Competition (Mottet et al., 2017)

Following Mottet et al. (2017, *Global Food Security*, 14, 1–8), `herdr` evaluates enterprise-level protein conversion efficiency on producing cohorts (`mature` and `slaughter`), integrating whole-herd feed intake (including `replacement` cohorts) allocated to edible protein by $AF_{\text{protein}} = 1 - AF_{\text{wool}}$:

1. **Total Protein Feed Conversion Ratio ($\text{Protein\_FCR}_{\text{total}}$):**
   $$\text{Protein\_FCR}_{\text{total}} = \frac{\text{Feed}_{\text{CP, total}} \times AF_{\text{protein}}}{\text{Protein}_{\text{total}}} \quad (\text{kg feed CP} / \text{kg edible protein})$$
2. **Human-Edible Protein Feed Conversion Ratio ($\text{Protein\_FCR}_{\text{human\_edible}}$):**
   $$\text{Protein\_FCR}_{\text{human\_edible}} = \frac{\text{Feed}_{\text{CP, human-edible}} \times AF_{\text{protein}}}{\text{Protein}_{\text{total}}} \quad (\text{kg human-edible feed CP} / \text{kg edible protein})$$
   * $\text{Feed}_{\text{CP, human-edible}}$ weights each ingredient's crude protein directly by the explicit `human_edible` column (`0` or `1`, also accepting fractions in $[0, 1]$) in `mapping.csv`, cleanly separating food competition from land-use classification (`land_type`).
   * **Default `human_edible` classification criterion in `mapping.csv`:** anchored on arable non-forage concentrates with $\text{economic\_allocation} > 0.33$ (`1` for primary cereal grains, pulses, soybean/linseed meals, and protein concentrates/isolates, plus commercial food-grade dairy feeds `casein` and `skimmed_milk`), while assigning `0` to all forages (including dehydrated alfalfa and forage meals; $h_e = 0$ per Wilkinson 2011; Mottet et al. 2017), secondary agro-industrial by-products ($\text{economic\_allocation} \le 0.33$, such as cereal straw, hulls, pulps, brans, DDGS, and secondary oilseed cakes), biologically inedible or food-waste items (whole cottonseed, vetches, acorns, bakery/bread by-products), internal suckled milk, and non-agricultural additives (urea, minerals, synthetic amino acids).
   * When $\text{Protein\_FCR}_{\text{human\_edible}} < 1.0$, the enterprise is a **net producer** of crude human-edible protein relative to competing human-edible feed protein consumed.
3. **DIAAS-Adjusted Edible Protein Conversion Ratio ($\text{EPCR}_{\text{DIAAS}}$) and Protein Quality Ratio ($\text{PQR}$):**
   Following **FAO (2013)** and **Ertl et al. (2016a, 2016b)**, `herdr` also accounts for differences in indispensable amino acid profiles and true ileal digestibility between plant feeds and animal-source foods using the untruncated **Digestible Indispensable Amino Acid Score (DIAAS, `0.5–3 yr` child reference pattern)**:
   $$\text{EPCR}_{\text{DIAAS}} = \frac{\text{Feed}_{\text{HDP}} \times AF_{\text{protein}}}{\text{Animal}_{\text{HDP}}} = \frac{\text{Protein\_FCR}_{\text{human\_edible}}}{\text{PQR}}, \qquad \text{PQR} = \frac{\text{DIAAS}_{\text{output}}}{\text{DIAAS}_{\text{input}}}$$
   where $\text{Feed}_{\text{HDP}}$ weights each human-edible feed ingredient's crude protein by `diaas_pct / 100` from `mapping.csv` (backbone: Ertl et al., 2016b, Table 4, supplemented by Ertl et al., 2016a, Rutherfurd et al., 2015, Cervantes-Pahm et al., 2014 harmonized via `48/57`, Herreman et al., 2020, and Nosworthy et al., 2018), and $\text{Animal}_{\text{HDP}}$ weights commercial animal protein streams by species-specific DIAAS values from **Ertl et al. (2016b, Table 5)**: cow milk (`115.9%`), sheep milk (`109.1%`), goat milk (`123.5%`), beef (`109.3%`), sheep/goat meat (`116.8%`), pork (`113.9%`), chicken meat (`108.2%`), and whole egg (`116.4%`).
   * **Transparency notes:** (i) Following Ertl et al. (2016b, Section 2.6), when $\ge 80\%$ (but $< 100\%$) of human-edible feed CP has a DIAAS entry, the weighted-average DIAAS of known ingredients is applied to total human-edible CP (emitting a warning whenever $> 5\%$ lacks DIAAS, and returning `NA` if $< 80\%$ is covered); (ii) `EPCR_DIAAS` uses weighted-average ingredient DIAAS at the farm gate (raw feedstuffs, without modeling cereal–legume amino acid complementarity in mixed human diets) and untruncated $> 100\%$ scores for animal products (reflecting their ability to complement lower-quality plant proteins in mixed diets); therefore, `EPCR_DIAAS` is always reported alongside unadjusted `Protein_FCR_human_edible` and `Protein_FCR_total`.
